object_types.name: Customer
object_types.definition: A person or organization who places orders; identified by a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order.
Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.
In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients."

object_types.name: CustomerId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a customer in the CRM system.

source_references.excerpt: Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

object_types.name: CustomerName
object_types.definition: The text name of a customer.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every customer has a name. It's just a text field.

object_types.name: Order
object_types.definition: A purchase order placed by a customer; identified by an order number.

source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order. Every order belongs to exactly one customer, and customers can place multiple orders over time.
Each order has an order number. That's the primary identifier.

object_types.name: OrderNumber
object_types.definition: The primary identifier value for an order.

source_references.excerpt: Each order has an order number. That's the primary identifier.

object_types.name: OrderStatus
object_types.definition: The status of an order, restricted to a fixed set of values.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, an order has a status. The possible values are: pending, confirmed, shipped, and delivered. Every order must have a status.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: A product that can appear on order lines; identified by SKU.

source_references.excerpt: An order contains one or more products. Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity.
By SKU -- a unique stock-keeping unit code.

object_types.name: Sku
object_types.definition: The unique stock-keeping unit code identifying a product.

source_references.excerpt: By SKU -- a unique stock-keeping unit code.

object_types.name: Quantity
object_types.definition: The quantity of a product specified on an order line.

source_references.excerpt: Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity.

Should this be enforced as a strict business rule?

ambiguities.description: Customer vs Client: the billing system's 'client' concept is defined differently (only counted once paid) than CRM's 'customer'. It is unclear whether Client should be modeled as a distinct subtype/entity with its own lifecycle state (e.g., paid status) rather than treated as a pure alias of Customer.

source_references.excerpt: For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: No temporal/history tracking is mentioned for Order status changes (pending -> confirmed -> shipped -> delivered). Is only the current status stored, or does the business need to track status history over time?
